subject: Follow-up: MedSync tenancy concerns and proposed mitigation plan
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Susan Park <susan.park@medsync.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: MedSync tenancy concerns and proposed mitigation plan

Hi Susan —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed path forward so we stay coordinated: 

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Primary requirement: predictable tail latency for live clinician-facing requests (p95 < 150ms).
- Data isolation: patient PHI must not leave your VPC or managed private environment.
- Concern about noisy neighbor behavior on shared pools; want clarity on isolation guarantees and mitigation.
- Procurement wants a simple SLO + escalation ladder to include in the contract.

Proposed next steps from Redwood: 
1) Send a short risk matrix that maps concerns (noisy neighbor, KV cache leakage, burst capacity) to mitigation options across Hosted / Dedicated / Private. See attached "medsync-tenancy-risk-matrix.xlsx".
2) Schedule a 1-hour technical deep dive with Vivek (runtime), Ben (ops) and your infra team next week to walk isolation controls and fallback patterns. Proposed slots: Tue/Wed morning PT.
3) We'll draft a contract appendix with the SLOs discussed and a runbook for degraded-mode fallback.

If that sounds right, I'll book the tech deep dive and loop in Procurement for contract timing.

Thanks,
Grace
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Attachment: medsync-tenancy-risk-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet summary — 3 tabs)

From: Dr. Susan Park <susan.park@medsync.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: MedSync Ops <ops@medsync.io>, Procurement <procurement@medsync.io>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: MedSync tenancy concerns and proposed mitigation plan

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the recap. The summary is accurate. A few clarifying Qs before the deep dive so we can prep our infra folks: 

1) On Hosted API: do you have concrete p95 latency SLO numbers under multi-tenant load for the models we discussed (redwood-small-8b and redwood-medium-30b)? We need real-world benchmarks showing percentiles under mixed workloads.
2) For KV/prefix caching: is customer KV segmented per tenant or is there a shared cache with namespace keys? We want to ensure no cross-tenant cache contamination.
3) For Dedicated: what isolation guarantees do you provide during noisy bursts (e.g., another customer's traffic pegging the GPU)? Does Redwood reserve CPU/GPU headroom or rely on queuing?

Also, Procurement asked that the contract appendix include an SLA definition for "service degradation" and a simple credit table. Can your team propose language for that appendix?

I'll review the attached matrix this afternoon. Please cc Vivek/Bob from infra on the deep dive invite — they'll want benchmarks.

Best,
Susan
CTO, MedSync Health
susan.park@medsync.io

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Susan Park <susan.park@medsync.io>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: MedSync tenancy concerns and proposed mitigation plan

Hi Susan and team —

Answering your questions at a high level so the deep dive is focused: 

1) Hosted API latency: our public benchmark for redwood-small-8b under mixed multi-tenant traffic shows median ~40ms, p95 ~160ms in the region we discussed. For redwood-medium-30b, median ~90ms, p95 ~320ms. Those numbers are for our current hosted clusters with autoscaling and continuous batching — but they can vary with prompt length and concurrency. We'll bring live traces to the call.

2) KV/prefix caching: customer state is namespaced per tenant; there is no cross-tenant KV leakage. We use tenant-specific cache keys and per-tenant TTLs. I'll walk through cache partitioning and eviction policies.

3) Dedicated isolation: for Dedicated pools we allocate GPU capacity per customer and enforce share policies. We protect throughput with two mechanisms: (a) reserved GPU slots and (b) request-level QoS that deprioritizes non-critical work during contention. In addition, we support preemptible burst lanes and strict node pinning for customers who need physical isolation. They'll see near-native latency in Dedicated and full control in Private.

SLA appendix: attached is a brief starter (redwood-deploy-options-brief.pdf) that includes a proposed degradation SLA and a credits table you can iterate on. Ben / Marissa: can you take the lead on the contract language and send a first draft by EOD Friday?

Thanks — Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-deploy-options-brief.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Susan Park <susan.park@medsync.io>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: MedSync tenancy concerns and proposed mitigation plan

Susan —

Quick update: I've drafted a short SLA appendix and a simple credit table for "service degradation" and attached the spreadsheet risk matrix updated with mitigation owners. The SLA includes:
- Availability SLOs for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (availability % and p95 latency targets)
- Definitions for "service degradation" (two tiers: reduced throughput and elevated latency)
- Credit calculation examples (percentage of monthly bill)

Link to draft contract appendix: https://drive.company/drive/folders/1a2b3c-medSync-PoC-docs

I'll schedule the tech deep dive for Wed 25 Aug 2027 at 10:00 AM PT. Vivek will demo the runtime isolation traces and we'll walk the risk matrix tab-by-tab. Please confirm attendees.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Dr. Susan Park <susan.park@medsync.io>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: MedSync tenancy concerns and proposed mitigation plan

Please include a short agenda in the meeting invite: 1) isolation demo (20m), 2) risk matrix walkthrough (20m), 3) contract appendix Qs (15m), 4) next steps/PoC scope (5m).

Talk then,
Susan
